title: Macklemore stages charity stadium concerts to raise funds for Palestine
content: US rapper Macklemore is staging charity stadium concerts intended to raise money for Palestine, as reported in an Arts24 music show hosted by Jennifer Ben Brahim. The segment highlighted the initiative among other weekly music releases and news.
summary: US rapper Macklemore is performing charity stadium shows. The concerts are intended to raise money for Palestine.
author: France 24

title: Israel election forces expats to fly home as voting abroad is prohibited
content:
Israel’s election rules require voters to be physically present in the country, meaning Israelis living abroad must travel home to cast a ballot. Tens of thousands of expatriates are expected to make the trip, and supporters of opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot have already gathered at Tel Aviv airport’s arrivals area.  

A “Fly and Vote” initiative is coordinating these journeys, despite a recent petition by Prime Minister Netanyahu’s Likud party to limit such travel that was rejected. Polls suggest a close contest, and each vote is seen as potentially decisive for the next prime minister.
summary: Israelis cannot vote from abroad, so tens of thousands of expats are expected to fly home for the election. At Tel Aviv airport, supporters of opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot are waiting, helped by a “Fly and Vote” initiative after a Netanyahu‑Likud petition to restrict the travel failed.
author: France 24

title: Harry Kane ends 25-year Ballon d'Or drought; Alexia Putellas wins third women's award
content: Harry Kane was named the Ballon d’Or winner on Monday, becoming the first Englishman to claim the award in 25 years after scoring 73 goals for club and country during the previous season. In the women’s category, Alexia Putellas secured her third Ballon d’Or, following Barcelona’s Champions League triumph and ending teammate Aitana Bonmati’s three‑year hold on the prize.
summary: Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season. Spain’s Alexia Putellas claimed her third women’s award after helping Barcelona win the Champions League, ending teammate Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign.
author: France 24

title: Flavio Bolsonaro vows opposition after Supreme Court travel ban
content: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said a Supreme Court justice barred him from leaving the country after he narrowly lost to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. He refused to concede defeat, denounced the travel ban as intimidation and pledged to challenge the election results while leading the opposition.
summary: Presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said a Supreme Court justice barred him from leaving Brazil after he narrowly lost to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. He refused to concede defeat, called the order intimidation, and said he will challenge the election results.
author: France 24

title: US Trade Rep Jamieson Greer says $3.4B Airbus loan threatens US‑EU tariff truce
content: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned on Monday that a €3.4 billion loan from the European Investment Bank to Airbus could threaten the tariff truce between Washington and Brussels. Greer said his office has received no details about the financing, which was announced in June, and urged the EU to resolve the issue promptly.
summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned that a $3.4 billion European Investment Bank loan to Airbus could jeopardise the tariff truce between Washington and Brussels. He said his office had received no details about the financing announced in June and urged the EU to resolve the matter quickly.

title: Kylian Mbappe loses two major Chinese sponsorships over Mao Zedong joke
content: French footballer Kylian Mbappé lost two Chinese sponsorships on Tuesday after a video showing him apparently joking about former leader Mao Zedong spread online. Energy‑drink producer Dongpeng and dairy company Mengniu announced they had terminated their partnerships, saying the remarks offended Chinese national sentiment.
summary: Kylian Mbappe was dropped by two major Chinese brands on Tuesday after a video showing him appear to joke about Mao Zedong circulated online. Energy drink giant Dongpeng and dairy producer Mengniu said they terminated their partnerships, citing remarks that offended Chinese national sentiment.
author: France 24

title: Israel holds first election since Oct. 7 Hamas attack, Netanyahu faces test

title: Dr. Michaela Musilova leads five-day underwater analog astronaut mission at Jules' Undersea Lab
content:
Dr. Michaela Musilova recently led a five-day simulated space mission called SEA STAR in the Jules’ Undersea Lab, a research station located 22 feet (6.7 meters) underwater near Key Largo, Florida. As an analog astronaut, Musilova participated in a mission designed to replicate the living and working conditions of astronauts on the International Space Station, as well as future missions to the moon and Mars. To enter and exit the station, crew members must scuba dive, and participants must remain underwater for at least 24 hours in a state of saturation to qualify as aquanauts. Musilova, who has commanded nearly 40 simulated space missions in various facilities worldwide, noted that while most previous missions were conducted on land, underwater operations carry significantly higher risks during spacewalks and maintenance activities.

The SEA STAR mission required over a year of organization to assemble the correct team, research projects, and funding. The crew consisted of experienced analog astronauts and divers, including Paul Bakken, an experimental engineer who served as Executive Officer and handled logistics. Dr. Brandy Nunez acted as the Health and Safety Officer, overseeing crew wellbeing while conducting microgreens research. Jenn Pint, an industrial safety expert, served as Mission Specialist and led a project in collaboration with Interstellar Performance Labs to develop a taxonomy for analyzing environmental and crew interaction factors. Musilova’s primary responsibilities as Commander included ensuring the crew’s safety, health, and morale, while also managing the mission schedule and conducting her own research and educational projects.

Due to the elevated health and safety risks associated with the underwater environment, the team adhered to stricter procedures than those required for land-based analog missions. This rigorous protocol was intended to make the experience more similar to actual astronaut missions in space. The underwater setting also enabled the performance of neutral buoyancy experiments during simulated spacewalks and allowed for scientific research focused on the effects of high atmospheric pressures on humans. The Jules’ Undersea Lab also functioned as a Mission Control Center on land, monitoring and assisting the underwater crew throughout the duration of the mission.

Musilova described feeling nervous prior to the mission, citing potential scenarios such as gear malfunctions or storms forcing an evacuation. Despite these concerns, she trusted her crew’s ability to problem-solve and face challenges, mirroring the resilience required of astronauts in space. The planned experiments ranged from cognitive research under pressure to testing environmental student sensors. As she prepared to dive for the five-day duration, Musilova focused on the positive aspects of the mission, eventually feeling calm as she submerged herself to begin the intense underwater operation.
summary: Dr. Michaela Musilova served as Commander for the SEA STAR mission, where a crew lived in an underwater habitat near Key Largo, Florida, to simulate space conditions. The five-day expedition involved performing scientific research and neutral buoyancy experiments while adhering to strict safety protocols.

title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
content:

The 63-year-old manager initially remained seated in the shadow of the bench when Kylian Mbappé scored the first goal but reacted dramatically to the second, which secured the win with time running out. Mourinho threw himself onto the grass, sticking his tongue out and pumping his fists, while his substitutes joined the players in sprinting toward the south-west corner of the stadium.

The celebration took place in the same location where Mourinho’s managerial career began, a detail highlighted as a symbolic return to form. In the stands, a small group of Madrid fans in a glass box celebrated enthusiastically, while a thousand phones were raised in the main stand. The match concluded with three points for Real Madrid, capping off a night that included earlier controversies such as a press conference no-show and a printout incident within Mourinho’s first 100 days in charge.

Goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was unable to play in the match due to flu, waking up ill on the morning of the game. He watched his teammates from the sofa at home in Boadilla, 600 kilometers west of the stadium, reportedly wrapped in a blanket and holding a cup of Lemsip. title: Show HN: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT
content:
Christian has introduced Hob, a new open-source project developed over the past few weeks. The application is a free, MIT-licensed desktop tool available for Mac, Windows, and Linux. Its primary function is to process user files similarly to the Claude and ChatGPT desktop applications, but it operates using open-weight models that run locally on the user’s computer. Currently, Hob supports the Gemma 4 and gpt-oss models. The developer emphasizes that all chats and files remain on the user’s system, with the only online components being optional web search and user-added MCP connectors.

Key features of Hob include an automated system that identifies the best open-weight model for the user’s hardware upon installation. The app can write sandboxed Python code for tasks such as data processing, document conversion, and graphing. It also incorporates built-in web search powered by SearXNG, Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, image recognition, and create, read, update, and delete (CRUD) capabilities for the local filesystem. The application is designed to function fully offline without an internet connection.

Christian stated that the project was initiated after testing various local AI applications, which he found lacked the ability to effectively manage files, images, and code execution. He noted that existing solutions often limited users to pasting plain text into small context windows, which failed with larger files, or defaulted to hosted models, undermining the privacy benefits of on-device processing. Some advanced open-source alternatives also tended toward account-based or open-core business models.

Technically, Hob is built using Electron bridged with llama.cpp running in its own process. During initial load, the system detects compatible graphics cards and defaults to CPU-only processing if none are found. Code execution occurs in a restricted sandbox that limits writing to the chat’s folder and blocks network access unless explicitly permitted, utilizing sandbox-exec on macOS, Landlock on Linux, and a low-integrity process on Windows. Image processing is handled by a small Qwen3-VL model, while dictation uses a local Whisper model.

The developer identified getting smaller models to use tools reliably as the most challenging aspect of development, noting issues with 4B models failing to call tools or entering infinite loops. He addressed this by building guards rather than relying on prompt tweaks. Christian acknowledged that local models are generally weaker than frontier cloud models but argued that for most common tasks, systems with 16 GB or more of RAM perform well, approaching the quality of hosted frontier models when equipped with a GPU or additional memory.
summary: Hey HN, I'm Christian and this is a new OSS project I've been noodling on for the last couple of weeks. Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that works on your files the way the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps do, except the model runs on your own computer.

title: Magic State Cultivation Achieves 0.9999 Fidelity on Superconducting Processor
content:
Researchers have demonstrated magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor, offering an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols for fault-tolerant quantum computing. The study, published in Science, addresses the significant cost associated with non-Clifford gates in most quantum error correction architectures. By implementing cultivation that includes code-switching into a surface code, the team developed a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity.

The experimental results show that the cultivation process reduces errors by a factor of 40. The method achieved a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1), while retaining 8% of the attempts. These findings experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to a critical challenge in quantum computing. The research was also highlighted in a 2026 Google blog post.
summary: Researchers experimentally implemented magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor, including code-switching into a surface code. The protocol reduced errors by a factor of 40 and achieved a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) while retaining 8% of attempts, demonstrating the viability of magic state cultivation.

title: Real-life Scottish surgeon Joseph Bell inspired Sherlock Holmes
content:
Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s creation of Sherlock Holmes, a character featured in numerous novels and films, was inspired by Joseph Bell, a renowned surgeon at the University of Edinburgh. Bell taught Doyle during the author’s time as a young medical student. This connection is the focus of a new biography titled Sleuth-Hound: The Case of the Real Sherlock Holmes, written by medical historian Lindsey Fitzharris.

Fitzharris is described as a noted science communicator with an interest in the medically macabre. Her previous works include the 2017 biography The Butchering Art about Joseph Lister, and the 2022 book The Facemaker, which details the work of World War I surgeon Harold Gillies. In 2020, she hosted the Smithsonian Channel documentary The Curious Life and Death Of…, where she conducted virtual autopsies, experimented with blood samples, and interviewed witnesses to investigate famous deaths, including those of Pablo Escobar and Harry Houdini. title: 71-Year-Old Korean Farmer's Eyes Plucked of 11 Pregnant Worms Before Larvae Release
content:
A 71‑year‑old crop farmer in South Korea sought treatment at an eye clinic after two months of discomfort, redness, and blurred vision in both eyes. Ophthalmologists found multiple mobile, whitish roundworms on the surface of the cornea. The patient reported a sensation of something stuck in his eyes. Examination revealed enlarged blood vessels in the conjunctiva and erosion of corneal cells, likely caused by the parasites.

The doctors administered a topical anesthetic to numb the eyes and then removed the worms one by one with fine forceps. They extracted 11 living, wriggling worms, each ranging from 11 to 22 mm in length. At the time of extraction, many of the female worms were pregnant, and the patient narrowly avoided having the larvae released directly into his eyes. The case was documented in a report published in the New England Journal of Medicine.
summary: A 71‑year‑old crop farmer in South Korea had 11 live worms removed from his eyes after two months of discomfort. The worms, many of which were pregnant, were plucked out by ophthalmologists before they could release larvae, and the patient’s cornea had been eroded by the helminths.

title: Microsoft to Offer Voluntary Buyouts to 60,000 Employees Across Four Countries
content:
Microsoft announced on Monday that it will offer voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees—about a quarter of its global workforce—according to CNBC. The company says the buyout program is an opportunity for employees who may already be considering career moves outside Microsoft.

The voluntary exit offer (VEO) will be available to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Eligibility is limited to staff at level 70 or below, with internal rankings that place levels 65–67 in principal positions and levels 68–70 at the partner/distinguished level. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said that eligible organizations were chosen “based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.”

Microsoft did not provide a direct reason for the new package, but the move comes after the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data‑center buildout. The VEO is the second voluntary workforce reduction Microsoft has run in 2026. In April, the company offered a voluntary retirement package to 8,750 U.S. employees, and in July the Xbox division laid off 3,200 workers—about 20 percent of its gaming division. CNBC reports that about 30 percent of employees who received the retirement offer accepted it, reducing the impact of the planned layoffs.

This latest offer expands the voluntary reduction effort to a much larger potential pool, giving a broader range of employees the chance to exit the company on their own terms.
summary: Microsoft will offer voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 employees, about a quarter of its global workforce, in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Eligible employees are at level 70 or below and may have been considering career moves outside the company.

title: Donnie Darko Celebrates 25th Anniversary as Sci-Fi Cult Classic
content: "Have you ever seen a portal?" The term "cult classic" has been loosely bandied about in cinematic circles until its definition has diluted into nothingness, but never has it been more appropriately applied than to director Richard Kelly’s strange psychological sci-fi thriller, "Donnie Darko", which celebrates its milestone 25th birthday today. Starring Jake Gyllenhaal, Drew Barrymore, Mary McDonnell, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Patrick Swayze, Jena Malone, and Noah Wyle, "Donnie Darko" was released on Oct. 26, 2001, into an unstable world still shocked by the catastrophic Sept. 11 terrorist attacks less than two months earlier. The thrust of the narrative revolves around an alternative universe accidentally forming via a supernatural anomaly after a jet engine falls off a commercial airliner and crashes through the roof of a suburban Virginia home, landing in the bedroom of our troubled title character. As the frightening phantom of Frank the Bunny warns, this parallel reality has a ticking clock that’ll result in its imminent collapse in just 28 days, 6 hours, 42 minutes, and 12 seconds. From the haunting voice telling our heroic teen, "Wake up, Donnie," as the grandfather clock in the Darko residence ominously chimed midnight, to its exploration of the nature of mental illness, time travel paradoxes, fraudulent motivational speakers, teenage angst in the 1980s, and the logistics of interdimensional portals, "Donnie Darko" became an ideal parable for turbulent times. But Kelly's post-modern sci-fi fantasy emerged on the big screen when there existed a pervading fear of gathering in large groups as America was just beginning to recover and process the atrocities committed on 9/11. Newmarket Films was perplexed on precisely how to market the movie, as it is such a unique combination of genres that forges something far greater than the sum of its parts. Throughout that entire fall, "Donnie Darko" came and went in multiplexes with barely a whisper, pulling in just over $500K off of a meager $4.5 million budget. Years later, it would become a bona fide word-of-mouth sensation via several re-releases, home video editions, and further experiences in regularly sold-out midnight screenings on its way to earning cult status. "Donnie Darko" celebrates its 25th anniversary on Oct. 26, 2026. (Image credit: Newmarket Films) It's a deeply personal film that will affect any viewer who allows its meticulously slow build to seduce them into its dreamlike sphere. Much has been debated and discussed about its many metaphors and symbolism, which employed elements of a splintered universe long before the multiverse was hijacked by Hollywood superhero spectacles. It’s a raw meditation on death more than anything, and its labyrinth of quantum entanglements feeds our existential core. "I remember pulling over to the side of the road to finish reading Richard's script and being mesmerized," Gyllenhaal told The Guardian. "It was clearly influenced by classic directors—Ron Howard, Steven Spielberg—but with this strange psychosis. It beautifully captured the experience of moving into adulthood: the world that felt so solid becoming movable and liquid. I thought, “This is what my adolescence felt like,” although I don’t speak, and have never spoken to, rabbits." Kelly was just 23 years old when he penned the "Donnie Darko" screenplay in only 28 days based on his own adolescence growing up in Virginia during the ‘80s. Coincidentally, that is the exact number of days Frank the Bunny declares will mark the end of the world, and it is also the same amount of time taken to complete the Southern California production shoot in 2000. Layered with ‘80s pop anthems like Echo & the Bunnymen's "The Killing Moon," Tears for Fears' "Head Over Heels," The Church's "Under the Milky Way," and Gary Jules' melancholy cover of Tears for Fears' "Mad World," Kelly's mysterious coming-of-age masterpiece still offers up a lucid nightmare tinged with a touch of consuming dread that lingers long after any screening. Kelly did release a director's cut in 2004 that adds extra footage and alters the soundtrack, but we recommend the original theatrical cut for the purist’s version of this classic! Considering today’s political strife, climate change concerns, AI paranoia, pharmaceutical overlords, and alienated youth culture, "Donnie Darko" and its 1988 election year setting still seems to have its finger on the zeitgeist's pulse, continuing to present provocative questions. This Halloween, check out "Donnie Darko's" mind-warping weirdness on this 25th anniversary occasion and let no one ever question your commitment to Sparkle Motion ever again!
summary: Director Richard Kelly's psychological sci-fi thriller "Donnie Darko" marks its 25th anniversary, having evolved from a modest box office debut into a word-of-mouth sensation. The film stars Jake Gyllenhaal and explores themes of time travel and mental illness through the story of a teen haunted by a giant rabbit.

title: Cassini takes first close‑up images of Titan on Oct. 26, 2004
content:
On October 26, 2004, NASA’s Cassini spacecraft captured the first close-up images of Saturn’s largest moon, Titan. This second flyby brought the spacecraft significantly closer to the moon than its initial pass on July 3, 2004, reaching a distance of 745 miles (1,200 kilometers) from Titan’s surface at its closest point. During this encounter, Cassini took hundreds of photographs, providing the highest-resolution views of the hazy moon available at the time.

The images revealed a large continent-sized region that scientists named Xanadu. This area featured bright spots hinting at a mountain range, along with a large basin and smooth plains. Although astronomers were already aware that Titan possessed an atmosphere, these detailed photos depicted a world with characteristics reminiscent of what scientists suspect a young Earth may have been like.

Data collected during this flyby, including instrument observations, enabled scientists to measure Titan’s atmospheric density and composition. This information was critical for planning the trajectory and descent of the Huygens probe, a European spacecraft that had hitched a ride to the Saturn system with Cassini. The Huygens lander subsequently touched down on Titan in January 2005 to examine the surface directly.

Over its 13-year mission at Saturn, which concluded in 2017, Cassini completed 127 close flybys of Titan. These repeated observations allowed for extensive study of the moon’s surface and atmosphere, building on the foundational data gathered during the historic October 2004 encounter.
summary: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft captured the first close‑up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan, flying 745 miles (1,200 km) from the surface. The images revealed a continent‑sized region called Xanadu, with bright features suggesting a mountain range, a large basin, and smooth plains.

title: Jimmy Webb Reflects on Wild Days and Writing Hits for Dolly, Glen, and Frank
content: From Wichita Lineman to MacArthur Park, he penned masterpieces. Then suddenly there’s a guy at the top of one of the poles. He’s got his phone, he’s talking to somebody and then … whoosh! He goes by. I never saw him again, but I never forgot him.” Webb immortalised the unknown telephone worker’s solitude (and imagined conversation with a distant lover) with a 1968 smash hit for Glen Campbell. “But you wouldn’t believe what some people thought it was about,” chuckles the songwriter, now a chatty, self-effacing 80-year-old, video-calling from his kitchen in Long Island. “One guy who wrote to me thought it was about a football lineman, and a woman thought the young man in the song gets electrocuted because ‘the Wichita lineman is still on the line’.”

title: ‘A cultural moment’: smash hit doc You Can See Everything continues to dazzle America
content: Nathan Fielder’s three-hour Elizabeth Holmes film has become a pop culture phenomenon but at a sold-out Times Square screening, no one was quite sure what to think In You Can See Everything, it’s Elizabeth Holmes’s partner who makes for 2026’s timeliest villain Secrets, lies and a shock A-list cameo: how You Can See Everything became the film of the year When I see a film a second time during its theatrical run, it’s typically to take someone else who hasn’t yet seen it, at least in part hoping to witness their reaction to a piece of art that excited or moved me in some way. Seeing Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder’s You Can See Everything a second time in New York City on a Saturday night was that impulse writ larger. This is a movie garnering a surprisingly sizable audience, and outsized audience reactions to go along with it; rewatching it in a full 300-seat auditorium offered the opportunity to re-experience that sense of discovery. Perhaps more to the point, almost everyone I knew had seen it already; all I could do was observe strangers. This documentary, peering into (and helping to create) a hall of mirrors around the famed med-tech scammer Elizabeth Holmes, has become the box office story of the fall, actually rising 25% on its second weekend to gross another $19.5m – a rare feat even given its expanded screen count. With over $45m in North America, it’s already one of A24’s biggest movies ever; it could wind up in the company’s top three, and way up on the list of the highest-grossing nonfiction features. If You Can See Everything isn’t quite an Obsession -level cash cow, it’s probably even more surprising that a three-hour documentary whose existence was only announced about eight weeks ago is on track to make more money than high-profile new releases like Practical Magic 2, Verity and Street Fighter, among others. It’s also outgrossed co-director Oppenheim’s fellow A24 surprise hit Primetime, which has the benefit of genuine movie star Robert Pattinson.
summary: ‘A cultural moment’: smash hit doc You Can See Everything continues to dazzle America.

title: Mac DeMarco dazzles Carnegie Hall with glowing melodies and shirtless antics
content:

The concert was marked by an energetic crowd of Gen Z fans, many accompanied by parental chaperones, and a group of bright‑eyed teens who had traveled from Wisconsin. Attendees were seen searching online for “Where to find Mac DeMarco after the concert” and joking about whether they might kiss The 1975’s frontman Matty Healy if given the chance.

The performance featured introspective anthems and a cover of a Michael Jackson song, underscoring DeMarco’s ability to blend familiar pop with his signature indie style. The show echoed the youthful excitement that first graced Carnegie Hall more than 68 years ago when Leonard Bernstein presented his first Young People’s Concert.

DeMarco’s early career, emerging from Vancouver in the early 2010s, was described as “party‑hardy” and “modern‑day Pigpen”‑like, with live sets that included Limp Bizkit covers and spontaneous audience make‑out sessions. The 2014 docu‑short Pepperoni Playboy captured this era, showing the artist and his band drinking champagne out of lobster shells and cliff‑diving amid a relentless touring schedule.

title: Lula Re‑elected in Brazil, Boosting Hope for Zero Deforestation by 2030
content:
The re-election of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Sunday has renewed optimism regarding the nation’s ability to meet its target of ending deforestation in all biomes by 2030. In a tight race against right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula secured an unprecedented fourth term in office. During his acceptance speech, the 81-year-old leader stated that Brazil would demonstrate how climate policy is handled in the country, noting that deforestation rates decreased annually during his previous four years in power.

Recent data from Brazil’s space agency indicates that forest-clearing in the Amazon reached its lowest level on record following the introduction of a deforestation action plan. This plan, introduced in 2023, constrained illegal cattle ranching from expanding into the rainforest. Carlos Nobre, a veteran Brazilian climate scientist and co-chair of the Science Panel for the Amazon, described the current situation as a “historic opportunity” to prevent the Amazon from reaching a tipping point where large sections could turn into savanna. He emphasized that while recent reductions in deforestation have been crucial, ending deforestation by 2030 and accelerating large-scale forest restoration remain urgent priorities.

Lula’s victory is also expected to bolster international fundraising efforts for rainforest protection. Brazil spearheaded the creation of the Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF), a fund designed to raise public seed capital for investment in financial markets, with returns paid to rainforest countries. Despite being a developing nation, Brazil has pledged $1 billion to the fund and aims to help reach a $10 billion goal from governments by the end of the year. Anders Haug Larsen, advocacy director at the Norway Rainforest Foundation, described the election result as a “relief” that makes it more attractive for donors to support rainforest protection.

On Monday, the day following the election, the Netherlands announced a €500-million contribution to the TFFF, subject to parliamentary approval and to be disbursed over ten years. This pledge brings the total committed to the fund to $7.8 billion. Norway’s climate minister, Sigrun Aasland, expressed hope that the $10 billion milestone could be achieved by year’s end. Brazilian officials, who have led fundraising efforts, reported ongoing conversations with potential donors including China, Korea, and Japan.

Despite the positive outlook for environmental policy, political challenges remain. Veteran diplomat Bráulio Ferreira de Souza Dias noted that right-wing pro-Bolsonaro lawmakers have gained more seats in both legislative chambers, creating a difficult political scenario. Observatório do Clima, a network of Brazilian green groups, stated that seven out of ten representatives and senators in the next legislature are likely to vote against the climate and environmental agenda. Sonia Guajajara, former minister of Indigenous Peoples, highlighted the need to consolidate the 20 indigenous territories created under the current administration, deeming them essential for tackling the climate crisis.
summary: Lula Re‑elected in Brazil, Boosting Hope for Zero Deforestation by 2030.

title: Typhoon Champi Declared Strongest Storm of Year So Far
content:
Typhoon Champi was declared the strongest storm of the year so far after recording sustained winds of 185 mph last week. From late Thursday to early Saturday, the typhoon battered Taiwan and Japan’s southern islands. Champi approached the east coast of Taiwan before the centre of the storm turned south along the Yilan County coastline, looping offshore and then tracking northwards away from the island. The storm brought gusts of up to 141 mph and 48‑hour rainfall totals of more than 620 mm to parts of Yilan.

So far, the death toll remains at one, with 527 reported injured. Widespread power outages affected more than 288,000 houses at one point, although most had since been reconnected. The storm has been downgraded to a tropical storm as it rapidly weakens to the south‑west of Japan’s mainland on Monday.
summary: One dead and 527 injured as winds of up to 185mph hit Taiwan and southern Japan, while Greece issues flood alerts Typhoon Champi was declared the strongest storm of the year so far after recording sustained winds of 185mph last week. From late Thursday to early Saturday, the typhoon battered Taiwan and Japan’s southern islands.

title: Fructose slows liver tumors in mice when key sugar-processing gene is missing, may lead to new treatments
content:
A new study led by researchers at City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK) has identified a previously unknown anticancer mechanism involving fructose. The research demonstrates that in the specific metabolic context of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), dietary fructose does not fuel tumor growth; instead, it suppresses it. This finding highlights a distinct metabolic role for fructose, which, despite its chemical similarity to glucose, is metabolized differently in the body.

The study underscores recent advances in understanding fructose metabolism and its regulatory functions in human health. By revealing how fructose can inhibit liver tumors in mice when a key sugar-processing gene is missing, the work positions fructose metabolism as a frontier topic in life sciences and medicine, potentially opening avenues for new treatments.
summary: Fructose is an important nutrient that, despite having a chemical structure very similar to that of glucose, is metabolized very differently in the body. Research into fructose metabolism and its regulation of metabolism in the human body has in recent years become a frontier topic in the life sciences and medicine.

title: Marine amphibian Gerrothorax maritimus discovered in Late Triassic China
content:
A fossil of Gerrothorax maritimus, a 74‑centimetre‑long marine amphibian, was uncovered in a national geopark in Guanling county, China.  The specimen, found by farmers, is almost perfectly preserved and represents the first evidence that an amphibian once adapted to fully oceanic life.  The discovery was reported by Ryosuke Motani of the University of California, Davis, and published in Nature Ecology & Evolution (DOI 10.1038/s41559-026-03209-9).

The researchers used strontium isotope ratios to confirm that the bones of G. maritimus carried a clear signature of seawater.  This indicates the animal grew to adulthood in the ocean rather than being a land‑dwelling organism washed in after death.  Palaeogeographic reconstructions place the site at least 30 kilometres from the nearest shoreline 237 million years ago, during the Late Triassic Period.  The fossil was recovered together with a 7‑metre ichthyosaur, Guizhouichthyosaurus, underscoring the marine context of the find.

Anatomically, G. maritimus was a flat, bottom‑dwelling ambush predator.  It possessed four legs and gills, features that distinguish it from fish and reptiles.  Its wide mouth and a robust hyoid bone in the neck suggest it used suction feeding, a strategy seen in modern bottom‑dwelling predators such as wobbegong sharks.  No evidence was found that the creature underwent metamorphosis, a common process in many modern amphibians.

The closest relative of G. maritimus, Gerrothorax pulcherrimus, lived in freshwater environments and was described nearly a century ago.  Motani argues that the marine lifestyle of G. maritimus was an accidental evolutionary outcome: the body armour that protected its freshwater ancestors also served as an impermeable barrier against saltwater.  He notes that “amphibious” does not necessarily mean the ability to live on land, citing modern newts that remain entirely aquatic.  John Long of Flinders University comments that, had reptiles not invaded the marine niche at the same time, amphibians might have diversified in the sea, but this did not occur.
summary: A 74‑centimetre fossil of the marine amphibian Gerrothorax maritimus was found by farmers in Guanling County, China, and identified as a bottom‑dwelling ambush predator from the Late Triassic seas. Isotope analysis showed the animal grew to adulthood in seawater, suggesting its strong body armour allowed it to survive in the ocean 237 million years ago.

title: Wind turbines kill nearly 19 million bats in US over 40 years
content: Hoary bats have been the worst affected of the 10 species the researchers studied Michael Durham/Nature Picture Library/Alamy Wind turbines have killed nearly 19 million bats in the US over the past four decades, according to the most comprehensive analysis of its kind to date. The problem seems to have worsened in recent years, with more than 1.5 million deaths now occurring annually. But there may be ways of making this green energy source safer for wildlife without overly affecting energy production. This data can help “advance research to really support effective conservation measures and science-driven decision-making in the future”, says Charles Labuzzetta at Fort Collins Science Center in Colorado. Endearing photos of bats show clever adaptations like long tongues Bats play a vital role in ecosystems, particularly by controlling insects like mosquitoes and moths that produce crop-killing caterpillars. But many species face growing threats from habitat loss, disease and human activities, with some now classified as threatened or endangered. Advertisement Wind turbines are one of these human-activity threats. Researchers have previously found large numbers of dead bats at wind farms during monitoring that is required to comply with wildlife protection regulations. But not all wind farms share their results, and monitoring methods vary from site to site, says team member Bethany Straw, also at Fort Collins Science Center. “We know bats are being impacted, but could we change the engineering or sites of a turbine to minimise those impacts?” she asks. “There’s been an increasing interest in this, but we just haven’t had the appropriate data yet.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Now, Straw, Labuzzetta and their colleagues have analysed 499 reports from wind farms across the 48 adjoining US states to estimate how many bats were killed by turbines from 1981 to 2024, focusing on 10 species. They used a statistical model that considered differences in how wind farms searched for dead bats, the size and design of their turbines, and the surrounding environment. Their results suggest that wind turbines killed an estimated 18.7 million bats between 1981 and 2024. Annual deaths seem to have exceeded 1.5 million from 2021 onwards, which may be the result of more wind turbines being installed. Hoary bats ( Lasiurus cinereus ) had the greatest losses, with an estimated 6.7 million deaths, followed by 5.8 million deaths among eastern red bats ( Lasiurus borealis ), 3.4 million among silver-haired bats ( Lasionycteris noctivagans ) and 1.5 million among big brown bats ( Eptesicus fuscus ). Wind farms near rivers and turbines with longer blades were linked to more deaths among certain species, while having more space between the blades and the ground may reduce the risk. Don’t forget birds and bats when renovating or building new homes As newer homes are built or older homes are renovated, empty attic spaces are disappearing – this eliminates a vital refuge for birds and bats during a biodiversity crisis The researchers aren’t sure why bats fly so close to wind turbines. Previous work suggests that migratory bats mistake the structures for trees, and approach them in search of food, shelter or mates. A recent European study also found that male bats sometimes sing courtship songs around turbines, potentially attracting females into the path of spinning blades. Differences in species prevalence and behaviours may partly explain why some seem to be more at risk than others. The researchers hope their findings will help wind farm developers protect bats by choosing safer locations and adjusting turbine designs. Research suggests that stripy wind turbines could prevent seabird collisions, for instance. Changing when turbines operate might also help. Research shows that temporarily shutting them down during periods of high bat activity, particularly in low winds, can substantially reduce fatalities with limited loss of electricity production. Journal Reference: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2612674123
summary: Wind turbines kill nearly 19 million bats in US over 40 years.
